newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey's Ciller says government change within days.
newsitem.headline: Turkey's Ciller says government change within days.

text.p: Turkey's Deputy Prime Minister Tansu Ciller said on Wednesday there would be a change of government within days to solve a row that has brought the Islamist-led coalition to the breaking point.
"A change of government is expected in the coming days," Ciller told deputies from her True Path Party (DYP) in parliament.

Ciller and Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan announced on June 1 that they would seek early elections to overcome a growing dispute with the secular establishment over demands for a crackdown on religious activism.
The two did not set a date for elections, which have to be approved by parliament, but a senior member of Erbakan's party said on Wednesday that elections were expected to take place in October.

Erbakan has said he would hand power to Ciller ahead of the elections. But talks between the coalition partners have become bogged down over the details of the swap, and this week they lost support from a far-right party for a caretaker government.
The strength of the 11-month-old coalition has been eroded by the defection of a number of DYP deputies, defections that have left the government with a razor-thin majority in parliament.

The coalition also is not assured of total support from conservative deputies from Ciller's party unhappy with the failure of their Islamist partners to meet the army-led demands for an Islamist crackdown.
Ciller said Erbakan's Islam-based Welfare Party (RP) bore some of the responsibility for the government situation.
"There have been provocations and wrongdoings by RP, opposition parties and those who want to run the parliament from outside," she said.
A key far-right party on Monday said it would not join a caretaker government sought by the coalition, jeopardising further the alliance's plans for early elections.
The government was relying on the support of the Grand Unity Party to get the needed parliamentary approval for early polls.
The main opposition Motherland Party has threatened to bring down the coalition in a censure motion.
